name: How does standard drywall compare to moisture-resistant drywall in kitchens?

mainEntity.name: How does standard drywall compare to moisture-resistant drywall in kitchens?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard drywall is suitable for dry living spaces, but kitchens experience frequent steam, grease, and temperature fluctuations that make moisture-resistant drywall the better choice. Moisture-resistant board has a water-repellent core and treated paper face that resist mold growth and sagging over time. Standard sheetrock is acceptable on kitchen accent walls well away from water lines, but opting for moisture-resistant panels behind sinks, dishwashers, and food-prep counters provides long-term protection against hidden leaks or high humidity. The small difference in material cost prevents costly water damage repairs later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Moisture-resistant drywall prevents mold and sagging from sink splashes and cooking steam, making it far superior to standard drywall for high-use kitchen areas.
